title: A New Formulation of Neural Data Prefetching
problem: Neural models for temporal prefetching suffer from large storage and latency costs, cannot generalize to unseen memory addresses, and are impractical for real hardware deployment. Traditional prefetchers fail on irregular memory access patterns.
motivation: Temporal data prefetchers can significantly improve performance by accurately predicting and fetching irregular data streams before they are needed.
method: The paper exploits a practical observation: in real programs, each memory address is typically followed by only a handful of other addresses. It builds a simplified model (called an abstraction) of memory addresses that captures this sparse pattern, then trains neural networks to predict which few addresses will likely be needed next. The method comes in two implementations: Twilight, which uses the full neural network, and T-LITE, a compressed version that generalizes to different program runs.
key_novelty: Because each memory address is usually followed by only a few others, an abstraction based on this sparse pattern makes neural prefetchers practical to deploy on actual hardware with significant improvements in speed and memory efficiency.
contributions: Problem reformulation showing that address successor patterns are sparse, enabling efficient neural solutions
Twilight prefetcher achieving 988x latency and 10.8x storage reduction over prior neural prefetcher Voyager
T-LITE compressed variant that generalizes across program runs with 1421x latency and 142x storage improvements
Demonstration of generalization to new temporal correlations not seen during training

metrics.speedup: 4% over Voyager, 12.2% over STMS, 8.5% over Domino, 5.9% over Triage
metrics.other: 988x latency reduction and 10.8x storage reduction vs Voyager; T-LITE: 1421x faster, 142x smaller

limitations: Twilight is noted as still not fully practical for hardware deployment; full generalization capabilities and training data sensitivity not thoroughly discussed.
primary_theme: Neural prefetcher design for practical hardware deployment
